text:
Evelyn (arch): Heads-up — we're planning the v1->v2 API migration next quarter. Quick proposal: allow per-tenant deprecation-override flags that can delay cutover per-route for a bounded window (30/60/90 days). Want input on operational surface and telemetry.

Jorge (eng-platform): +1 on tenant overrides. Implementation idea: flags stored in the config service (evaluated at request time). Do we scope to whole account or per-route?

Li (eng-infra): We need per-route. Some customers only use embeddings or the legacy rerank endpoints. Whole-account toggles will be too coarse.

Priya (product): Product asks for explicit opt-out windows (expires_at) and an email cadence so we can nudge customers. Also: UI needs to show which routes are still on v1.

Evelyn (arch): Agreed per-route with an expires_at. Operational note: per-route flags complicate routing decisions and SLO accounting. If a tenant opts out, we should route to a compatibility shim rather than keep old code paths forever.

Jorge (eng-platform): Shim approach sounds good — a lightweight translator that maps v2 payloads back to v1 shapes (and vice-versa for requests). Important: make shim stateless and idempotent. Perf estimate: ~5-10% CPU overhead per request and minor p99 latency bump in our bench. We'll gate the shim behind the tenant flag.

Li (eng-infra): Telemetry we must capture: shim.hits (by tenant + route), shim.latency.p50/p95/p99, shim.token.delta (tokens emitted vs tokens expected), and shim.error_rate. Also: slow-path tagging so we can alert on SLO regressions.

RolloutBot: Proposed rollout plan: canary 2% tenants -> 10% -> 25% -> 100%. Auto-rollback condition: shim.p99_latency_increase > 150ms sustained for 5m OR shim.error_rate > 1% for 10m.

Jorge (eng-platform): Rate-limit implications: shimming increases CPU and may raise concurrency pressure. Options: (a) rate-limit affected tenants proactively, (b) route shim traffic to a separate autoscaling pool, or (c) accept transient degradation and rely on autoscaler. I prefer (b) to isolate impact.

Priya (product): Also want an opt-in flow for customers who want more time (legal/compliance). We'll need a support/UI flow to request extended windows and a way to log approvals.

Evelyn (arch): Decision (tentative):
- Implement per-tenant, per-route override flags in config service with expires_at.
- Implement stateless compatibility shim that rewrites v2<->v1 exchange; shim enabled by flag.
- Route shim traffic to a dedicated autoscaling pool to limit blast radius.
- Add telemetry: shim.hits, shim.latency.p99, shim.token.delta, shim.errors, and tenant-level SLO deltas.
- Rollout via canary phases with RolloutBot rules.

Code snippet for config format (example):
```yaml
feature_flags:
  api_v2_grace:
    tenant: "tenant-123"
    routes: ["embed.*", "generate.create"]
    expires_at: "2025-07-01T00:00:00Z"
    reason: "legal extension"
```

Li (eng-infra): Action items:
- (Jorge) design shim API surface + perf bench (ETA 2w)
- (Jorge + Li) infra: dedicated shim pool + autoscaling policy (ETA 3w)
- (Priya) product: opt-out UI + support workflow + email cadence (ETA 2w)
- (Evelyn) produce a short runbook for rollback and tenant notifications (ETA 1w)
- (All) define exact telemetry tag keys and dashboard widgets (sync tomorrow 10:30am)

Jorge (eng-platform): I'll start a draft RFC with the shim interface and perf targets. Will include failure modes and circuit breaker suggestions.

Priya (product): Please cc support and legal on the RFC when ready. We'll prepare message templates for customers. :+1:

Evelyn (arch): Thanks all. If nobody objects in 24h we'll lock the decision and start implementation planning.

Jorge (eng-platform): No objections from me.

Li (eng-infra): 👍

Priya (product): 👍

RolloutBot: Canary job scheduled: start at 2025-04-07T02:00:00Z if RFC merged. Monitoring hooks: shim.* metrics tracked in infra-dash.
